To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the overexpression of a carboxyl-terminal fragment of the amyloid precursor protein in human neuroblastoma cells leads to a decreased rate of cell proliferation and the appearance of aberrantly processed amyloid precursor protein fragments.
the human neuroblastoma cells stably expressing the COOH- terminus of APP exhibit altered processing and decreased growth rates.

(1) the human neuroblastoma cells expressed several products of APP, (2) expression of APP in these cells resulted in a decrease in their growth rate, and (3) expression of APP led to a decrease in the levels of the native mRNA for APP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of a COOH-terminal region of the human amyloidal precursor protein (APP), in a human neuroblastoma (SK-N-MC) cell line.
the effects of the expression of a carboxyl-terminal region of the amyloid precursor protein on a human neural cell system.
the expression of APP and its fragments in a human neuroblastoma line and their possible role in neurotoxicity and neurotrophic function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of the carboxy terminus of APP in a heterogeneous human neuroblast cell line leads to the formation of several fragments, some of which are neurotoxic and may be involved in the etiology of Alzheimer's disease.

the expression of a carboxyl-terminal region of APP in a neuroblastoma cell culture results in the production of several aberrant products of APP which are neurotoxic and lead to a reduction of growth of the cells.
the overexpression of APP leads to aberrant processing of the protein and to selective neurotoxic effects in a heterogeneous culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
expression of a COOH-terminally truncated APP fragment in a neural cell line can lead to aberrant processing of APP and that this aberrant processing is neurotoxic.

the overexpression of the carboxy-terminal portion of APP in a heterogeneous culture neuroblastoma cell system leads to altered processing of APP and to a substrate-adherent, fibroblast-like morphology; these cells exhibit a decrease in the growth rate which is partially reversible by addition of conditioned medium.
the expression of the carboxy-terminal portion of APP in a heterogeneous culture system results in altered processing, decreased cell growth, and selective neurotoxocity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the overexpression of APP leads to altered cleavage and neurotoxicity.
overexpression of a carboxyl-terminal fragment of the beta- amyloid precursor protein in neuroblastoma cells leads to altered processing of the protein, decreased growth, and selective neurotoxicty.
the APP gene can be expressed in a heterogeneous culture and that expression of APP in this culture can lead to altered processing of APP.
